sb_prompt: WHAT SHORT AND LONG-TERM STEPS DO YOU AND THE OTHER CALLER THINK SHOULD BE TAKEN TO IMPROVE THE US BUDGET?
turns: Yeah, I'm at a library actually, but I'm pretty skeptical about all this budget talk. I mean, I know this old guy who lost his pension because of the cuts, so it's not exactly pretty. How about you? What do you make of it?

Haha, well, I'm a carpenter so I see it differently. My cousin's a teacher and she's fighting for her pay so she can afford rent, but honestly, I think we should probably just stop the waste first before we add anything else.

Waste? I guess I can see that, but honestly, you can't just stop the waste when people are actually starving. That guy I told you about... he didn't lose his pension because he wasted anything, his pension got slashed just to save money on corporate tax breaks.
That's fair, but then how do you stop the waste from things like all those unused building permits?
Well, but if we slash the grants to support small workshops like the one my brother runs, then he's out of a job too, and that's not waste, that's just throwing good people away.
Yeah, but can you stop the waste without hurting the grants too?
Look, it's not that simple, you can't just pick and choose what's "waste" without someone losing out.
I guess you're right, but where do we draw the line?

That's the thing, you can't really draw a line because a permit might be unused now but someone else needs it next week, and that whole point about corporate tax breaks is actually the biggest waste of all since that money just goes right out of the economy.
So what are you saying we actually do then?
I'm saying we fix the tax breaks first, because that's the easy waste, and then we figure out how to keep the rest of the grants safe.
That actually makes sense, I guess. Maybe we could tax the big corporations more to pay for the small stuff?
Yeah, that'd be a good start, maybe we could actually tax the big guys more to pay for the small stuff?
Yeah, I've got some ideas on that, but honestly it'd probably get stuck in committee somewhere.
Yeah, but I don't think it will get stuck if we just keep pointing out the biggest loopholes first.
Yeah, but do you think pointing at the loopholes is enough if the politicians don't have the guts to fight for it?
Pointing out the loopholes is the only way to make them care, otherwise the whole thing just gets ignored.
Yeah, but what if the politicians just say "we'll do it next year" every time?
Well, you can't let them wait forever, or people just stop trusting the system entirely.
I guess we'd need to keep the pressure up if we want anything to actually change.
Yeah, but if we just keep waiting for them to get brave, nobody's gonna trust the system ever again.
Yeah, but if we get too pushy, maybe they'll just find some other way to kill it before we even get started.
Yeah, but you can't just let them kill it all off before we get a word in.
Yeah, but how do we get them to actually listen without just making everyone mad?
Look, we don't have to be loud, just keep showing them that if they don't act now, more people like my brother and my friend will lose everything.
Yeah, but if everyone starts yelling, maybe they'll just dig in deeper and pass nothing at all.
Right, so we keep showing them who's actually hurting, but we do it quietly instead of just screaming.
Yeah, maybe a few quiet letters to their offices would work better than just yelling.
Yeah, write a few, but make sure you actually mention my brother's name so they can't just sweep it under the rug.
Yeah, but what if they just ignore the names and call it harassment?
Harassment is the last thing they want to hear, so we have to frame it as their own loss first.
Yeah, but how do we know we're not just making it worse for them instead?
That's the risk, but if you don't name names, they'll just call it a abstract problem and do nothing at all.
Yeah, but if you name names, don't you think they'll just make up some rule to say it's not actually a financial loss?
Look, I don't want to name names just to have them say "not a financial loss," but if we don't say who it is, they never admit it hurts anyone at all.
Yeah, but if we name too many people, won't they just say "that's not the priority" and move on?
If we don't say whose money is gone, they'll never admit it's a loss, so we have to name a few specific names to force them to face it.
Yeah, but if you just name one guy, won't they just say "that one exception doesn't count for everyone else"?
Then we pick just one name that hits the hardest, like my friend, so they can't say it's just an exception.
Yeah, but if you pick just one guy, don't you think they'll just say "that one exception doesn't count for everyone else"?
